_chunk_note: THE FACE'S MATERIAL ONLY: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission, a locally generated PMREM environment map, and an OPAQUE test-pattern stand-in behind the card so the frost's detail-destroying threshold can be measured. ⚠ RIM AND BEVEL STAY DIAGNOSTIC GREY — colouring them in the same chunk that introduces glass would mix two variables Carl could otherwise separate, and contradicts chunk 1's own argument that grey exists so a form defect cannot hide behind a plausible colour. ⚠ EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: the real logo backdrop and its colour movement (chunk 3), the filament (chunk 4), rollout and the Next step button (chunk 5), text on the card's face (parked, shared with the contact field), and ANY edit to the five live CSS cards.
_transmission_note: ⚠ THE TRANSMISSION PASS RENDERS opaqueObjects ONLY (three.module.js:18039), and the split at :8237 sends anything with transparent === true to the transparent list. So a material is excluded from what the glass can see if it is EITHER transmissive OR transparent. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (1) the stand-in must be transmission === 0 AND transparent === false — a 'stand-in opacity' rig control would silently break the effect with every assertion still green; (2) chunk 1's rim and bevel are ALREADY excluded during the entrance, because answer-card-canvas.tsx sets transparent = true at attach and holds it until the fade completes.
_refraction_note: ⚠ REFRACTION IS NEAR-INERT UNDER THIS CAMERA AND thickness/ior SHIP FIXED. An orthographic camera down -z gives v = (0,0,1) everywhere, so the crown centre is at normal incidence and refract() returns pure -z. Measured at ior 1.45 / thickness 6: displacement is 0.000px at the face centre and 0.801px at chunk 1's measured 23.70deg maximum tilt. Sub-pixel everywhere. Exposing thickness and ior as rig knobs would move numbers and change nothing on screen — this project's own logged trap. What WebGL buys here is blur that responds to real surface curvature and real lighting in one lit scene, NOT visible bending; that is what Carl should be asked to judge.
_standin_note: ⚠ A TEST PATTERN, NOT THE LOGO — and the swerve was forced by measurement. Revision 1 proposed the whole c2b mark behind one card at a claimed 4.24px thinnest stroke; that figure came from a SINGLE mid-line scan and is wrong. Scanning the whole mark: thinnest stroke is 14px of a 566px-tall mark (ratio 0.0247), which at the proposed 32px placement lands at 0.79px on screen. A 4px stroke needs the mark ~162px tall, 5x the face height. The chunk now ships parallel strokes at 2/4/6/8px and MEASURES the threshold, which hands chunk 3 arithmetic instead of a guess: a mark spanning the grid's 576px width gives a 7.18px stroke. Carl on the swerve: 'Setting the chunks is important, but something may arise in the process that we must swerve and be adaptable.'
